title: Aesthetics
subtitle: Social systems, identity, and the place of art and enchantment in avodah.
html:
From the newsletter, 2 October 2026.

There is a mechanism within social systems, and already we need to define some terms. A social system is an emergent sphere that arises from individuals, and then defines individuals. Every bubble is composed of the same anatomy: there is an inside, an outside, and a membrane that works to separate between inside and outside, a membrane that mediates what is allowed in. An example of a bubble is the human body that has an inside, an outside, and an immune system which polices the difference between the two. Any given cell also has this same anatomy. The cell wall is made of phospholipid bilayers with technology within that allows the controlled passage between inside and outside. Social systems also have a boundary, and the boundary excludes and includes.

But what does the social system do to the individual, or in other words, what is the consequence of a social system? Meaning, if there is a forest, and I name all the trees, the forest doesn’t change, and I have done nothing to it. I could disappear, along with my names, and the forest would be none the wiser. So let's say that there is a social system, why is that not the same as simply drawing a circle around a bunch of units that don’t care whether or not a circle has been drawn?

Well, the social system actually generates new anatomy within the individual, and that anatomy manages to interrelate and participate with so many other layers of systems that compose the individual, so much so that the process of generating a sense of what world one lives in is deeply colored and determined by this newly introduced anatomy.

Anatomy in the world of pure information is not local to biology. Anatomy refers to any data structure. Consider the example of a basketball game. The anatomy of that space defines what counts as meaningful, it bends the world temporarily into its own sphere of coherence. The color of one's eyes is not meaningful because in the anatomy of basketball’s meaning structures, there is no space to hold that information. A lot of information is excluded because of anatomical insensitivity: the fact that a hotdog is being eaten by 865 people is meaningless to the game. It is meaningful within the anatomy of the stadium as an object of commerce and consumption, in which universe the actual score of the game is meaningless data, at the very least in comparison to the number of hotdogs eaten.

Without the social system, the individual would not have an anatomy that absorbs a certain subset of information. The social system introduces identity.

It is of consequence to me if I am inside or outside. Now that the membrane of the social system defines the inside by metrics such as “has 15 million or more in the bank account,” it now becomes deeply important to have fifteen million, because being inside is important. Why is it important? Because my identity is that I am a wealthy person! If I don’t have the money, then I am not who I am, and if I am not who I am, then who am I?

So where the mental model stands is as follows: social systems are a bubble that define inside and outside and thus provide identity by populating the informational dimension of “I belong to this group” and “those people do not belong to this group, instead they belong to that group” and “to be part of this identity means you must have x y and z traits/possessions/manners/vernacular/perspective/etc, and so it is because I am identified with this identity, or would like to identify with it, that I strive for those things.”

You see how the anatomy of social systems and identity create a new dimension of inclusion or exclusion, a new dimension of information metabolism, that has its own reasoning and logic. Things which are inherently neutral inherit a valence from the social system. A surface of objects that was once flat bends into resistance and attraction by the social system.

The clothing of culture-society, most of all, is an arena of identity and social expression. The clothing of culture-society of course includes material visual products, but extends to linguistic forms and even thought forms. Your patterns of thinking are part of culture-societal clothing, and that might be surprising until you realize that your thinking is shaped by your speaking and your speaking is shaped by the external lifestyle you are dressed in.

I want to highlight the power of culture-society in excluding and including aesthetics, by highlighting how far aesthetic forms reach. These are not new thoughts or surprising thoughts, but it's worth speaking them out. Let’s take a wizard hat. Why does that conjure up an image in your head? Why do we have a communal sense of what this object is? Why might it be the case that in your mind, there is a pointy, blue hat with maybe some yellow stars on it? How did this object solidify into an abstraction, and lodge itself into the system of objects that populate being as a whole? It is not simply a hat, because the wizard hat belongs to the non-existent wizard. This is a figure that is rooted in the cast of medieval European characters, alongside the knight, which did exist, and other familiar Arthurian forms. But the wizard is a form that captures the aesthetic of magic and mystique, the cluster of forms that capture the otherworldly and arcane, and the power of the hidden forces that plausibly exist in the universe to make one into an insider that has the ability to do special things. Once the form of the wizard captures all these abstractions in the space of its oversized hat, they now become part of a coordinate in information space that begins neutral, but quickly becomes sorted out once identity gets its paws on it.

Let’s say, for example, you are somebody who loves mathematics. The mental capacity to internalize information through a mathematical framework, entering into the cerebral mindfields of pure mathematics, that is a magical experience. In a world without the wizard, those aesthetics might well have been worn by mathematicians, and in fact by Pythagoras, mathematics took on the religious fervor of a cult to the point that they swore by numbers! But now that wizards are associated with an order of thinking that is regressive and embodying of a worldview based on ignorant assumptions, assumptions that are de facto ridiculous because they were not achieved through the scientific method, now those aesthetics are foreclosed.

Let’s take another example that extends the extremes in both directions. It’s the 21st century, and the wizard form has been filtered through many layers and lands in the imagination of Walt Disney and his enterprise of aesthetic engineering, world engineering, creating new consciousness and effectively American consciousness, using a team of engineers – ahem, ‘imagineers’. So now the notion of magic is diffused and commodified through a known grammar of fantasy visuals and fantasy laws, magic is something that is an obviously different space, an obviously non existent escape space, a space we wish but alas ends with the movie, with the movie magic, with the animation, animating of forms that don’t exist, that don’t look like anything native to our reality.

Now, you are a Ben Torah, a Bat Yisrael, you are insulated from America, forget American culture, even the neutral modes of American thought without being plugged into her media is something from which you are pure. You might even speak in a language that to the average American sounds completely unintelligible, perhaps it’s a mix of Yiddish and Talmudic aphorisms and references to your own newly minted subculture, referencing your own system of media references and music. Now, the relationship you have to torah is in terms of old, snowy ghettoed Europe. It is in terms of a pure population that landed in New York and established New Vilna, pickles mayonnaise dynastic families and all. This is the insulation of your Torah, and the aesthetics of magic are already invalid. Nothing that isn’t part of the culture is permitted as a frame for the Torah participation. You want to look at Torah with those aesthetics? Even if those aesthetics were native to Yisrael originally, even if those forms were descendent through the generations, a primal engine of mythical context for our hopes and dreams, the soul of a yearning for Bayit Shelishi when magic will return to earth and the Doer of Miracles will be seen eye to eye once again, you are aligned with the outside and thus not an insider. Those forms, not inherently but because of an identity commitment, that would be unaligned with our separation from American mythologies. Are you an idiot? A believer in lies and fictions? A believer in magical thinking, in the word ‘magic’, in the experience of ‘enchantment’ and an earth of sparkles and a twinkle of youth in your eye unmurdered by prosaic mundanities that never seem to show up in the curation of Disney earth?

So it's not merely the notion of magic, but any aesthetic that is not the one preselected and predefined both in contrast and in perpetuating the form we are used to be the surrounding filament on avodah. I want to ask the question of what Avodah might look like if there is an opening up of our aesthetic rights. Do you realize the violence of Walter Disney and his slave, Michael “Mickey” Mouse? Our intellectual property has been stolen and now we are not permitted to develop an organic connection with the lubricating oil and hydrating sweetwater of a world model that is essentially magical and enchanting and beautiful, simply because he took those feelings and thoughts and embodied them in the cage of a visual grammar that is infantilizing and so obviously false such that we are led to throw out the baby with the bathwater. It is by displacing those structures into a world that is so far from ours that ours, in its contrast to the explicitness of Disney forms, looks dead and non-magical, mundane in comparison. Who can watch a Disney film and then go to the DMV? But the DMV, taking your kid to the pediatrician, doing carpool, having lunch, these moments have the potential to feel magical if we allow ourselves to understand that magic is not the Disney circus of sparkles and fairytales but instead looks like those daily activities. We take for granted that other humans are real, existing beings, and marriage?! The idea that you and an other fuse into one, reach heights of relationship and connection that dilate your contact with being beyond your wildest imagination – that is insane! And that itself, the robbing of romance, the robbing of relationship, the robbing of every stage of relationship, by an institution that turns life into a disgusting tragedy, that makes nobility and integrity into something to break and lay down, something that will inevitably break and remain broken.

So art and culture that might rhyme with klipah but which emerges out of the natural impulses from within kedusha, this is a region that is fruitful to explore, and to open up even the very possibility of using aesthetic immersion in avodah, these experiences must be interrogated. That interrogation is not going to take place here, but simply ask the question, what place does aesthetic, design and art have in one’s avodah? My point is to simply demonstrate that this line of questioning touches on deep nerve centers in being and should at the very least not be disregarded lightly.
